finding.claim: Configured max_auth_attempts (server/mod.rs:91, default 10 at :121) is never enforced. auth_attempts is incremented per USERAUTH_REQUEST and AuthRequest.rejection_count is incremented in reject_auth_request, but neither is compared to any limit. The only throttle is a sleep of auth_rejection_time (default 1s, server/mod.rs:112) per rejection, so one connection allows roughly 3600 password, publickey or keyboard-interactive guesses per hour with no disconnect.
finding.source: Unauthenticated remote client sending repeated SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST messages on one connection (encrypted.rs:88-98).
finding.sink: Authentication guess oracle: handler.auth_password (encrypted.rs:562), handler.auth_publickey (encrypted.rs:779) and auth_keyboard_interactive (encrypted.rs:641) are called for every attempt with no attempt cap.

trace.note: max_auth_attempts declared as the 'Maximal number of allowed authentication attempts' config field
default max_auth_attempts = 10
each USERAUTH_REQUEST is dispatched to server_read_auth_request with no pre-check on attempt count
self.common.auth_attempts += 1 with no comparison against config.max_auth_attempts
handler.auth_password called on every attempt
reject_auth_request
rejection_count += 1, never read (auth.rs:236 declares it, no reader in non-test code)
tokio::time::sleep_until(until) is the only rate limit, about 1s per attempt

finding.guards_checked: Grep across russh/src for max_auth_attempts and rejection_count (non-test): only the declaration, default and Debug impl of max_auth_attempts; no reader of rejection_count. Constant-time rejection timing (server/mod.rs:70-75, encrypted.rs:51-62) limits timing leaks but not guess volume. No disconnect after N failures found in encrypted.rs process_packet. Exploitability depends on whether the embedding application adds its own per-connection or per-IP limits.

finding.claim: For OpenSSH certificate auth the library verifies only the certificate's self-signature (cert.verify_signature) and its validity window. It does not check that the signing CA is trusted, that the certificate type is User rather than Host, that principals match the requested user, or critical options. Those checks are delegated to auth_openssh_certificate, whose doc (server/mod.rs:284-290) says only that 'signature has been verified and key ownership confirmed' and does not state that the signature is self-referential.
finding.source: Remote client presenting an attacker-generated certificate: attacker chooses the signing CA key embedded in the cert, principals and cert type, and the requested user name (encrypted.rs:523, decoded at :699-721).
finding.sink: Authentication success via handler.auth_openssh_certificate(user, cert) returning Accept, followed by server_auth_request_success and InitCompression (encrypted.rs:781-788).

trace.note: user name taken from the packet
PublicKeyOrCertificate::Certificate branch entered for an attacker-supplied cert
validity window checked (valid_after / valid_before)
cert.verify_signature(): proves only that the cert is consistent with its embedded signature key, not that the CA is trusted
possession of the cert's key checked over the session id and signature
handler.auth_openssh_certificate(user, cert) is the only trust decision
default implementation rejects, so the risk only exists when an application overrides it

finding.guards_checked: Validity window (encrypted.rs:702-711); self-signature verification (714); proof of key possession (774); default reject (server/mod.rs:296). Grep for principals, CertType and critical_options in non-test server/auth code returned no matches. Impact requires an application that overrides auth_openssh_certificate and accepts on verify_signature() alone or without principal, type or CA-pin checks. Rated medium on the library contract, not a confirmed exploit in a specific deployment.

finding.claim: Inbound CHANNEL_DATA that exceeds the advertised receive window is not rejected or dropped. adjust_window_size skips the decrement when data.len() > sender_window_size, and the caller still forwards the data to the application channel, so the window is not an enforced bound (RFC 4254 section 5.2). The library also keeps topping up the window (session.rs:301-311).
finding.source: Authenticated peer sending CHANNEL_DATA or CHANNEL_EXTENDED_DATA longer than the window it was granted (client/encrypted.rs:453-456, 475-478).
finding.sink: Data delivered to the application via chan.send(ChannelMsg::Data{..}) (client/encrypted.rs:469-471; the server path is the same at server/encrypted.rs:1024-1036).

trace.note: CHANNEL_DATA parsed; data length taken from the packet
enc.adjust_window_size(channel_num, &data, target) called
if data.len() > sender_window_size the decrement is skipped (comment says 'Ignore extra data' but nothing is dropped)
window is replenished to target when below target/2
data forwarded to the application regardless of the window outcome
application channel is a bounded mpsc (channel_buffer_size, default 100), so backpressure limits memory

finding.guards_checked: Bounded mpsc channel (channels/mod.rs:469) limits memory growth. Per-packet size capped by MAXIMUM_PACKET_LEN (cipher/mod.rs:313) and max packet size. Packet MAC verified before the data is used. Impact is protocol conformance and application quota bypass, not unbounded memory growth. Rated low.
